Impact has increased over the last 36 hours; our page said error rate for streaming clients jumped from 0.6% to ~8% and we have a few key patient-facing workflows affected.

Examples: request IDs 6f2b9a0a, 6f2b9a0b, 6f2b9a1e — all around 2027-04-03T16:47Z. Attached are a HAR and a small pcap. You can see repeated TCP retransmits followed by a quiet period.

Partial ask: can you confirm whether recent routing/edge config or keepalive defaults changed on your side? Our infra team rolled a proxy change yesterday but the timing aligns with a Redwood rollout tracked in your dashboard (model: rwd-open-3b-quant).

This is high priority for Halcyon — we have clinicians depending on streaming latency. Please advise immediate mitigations we can apply and next steps for a durable fix.

Thanks,

FYI — initial triage notes after a quick look at the logs Dawn attached:
- Multiple sessions show the HTTP response has Transfer-Encoding: chunked and then long gaps with no bytes sent. Not all requests fail; failure ratio matches Halcyon's reported ~8%.
- Edge (nginx) upstream shows keepalive pconn drops around the same timestamps; internal metrics show a spike in socket retransmits and a small number of reset streams.
- No obvious new model deployment in the last 48h on the customer-facing pool — but we did push a kernel selection tweak to the rwd-open-* family on 2027-04-02 03:22Z to prefer a different GEMM kernel on a subset of nodes. That could change per-token CPU scheduling at high concurrency.

Short mitigation proposal (quick):
1) Route Halcyon traffic to an alternate stable pool (no kernel tweak) — we can do this in 15–30 mins if capacity allows.
2) Temporarily disable streaming chunking at the proxy layer for Halcyon (force single-chunk response) — avoid pauses but increase latency and memory.
3) If neither is viable, advise customer to use the non-streaming endpoint as Aditya suggested.

I'll attempt a targeted re-route and keep you posted.

—Marissa
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Adding technical details from infra/serving runbook and what I see in the PCAP:
- The pcap shows repeated small TLS record writes from client then a 10–40s pause with no data from our server before the server emits the next chunk. The server-side TCP stack is not closing the connection; it's just not sending.
- Kernel selection tweak pushed 04-02 was limited to a small canary (15% of serving nodes). Looking at Halcyon's target IPs, ~40% of their traffic landed on canary nodes in that time window — unlucky sampling.
- I suspect a subtle backpressure interaction: a combination of a changed prompt-engine scheduling (longer CPU-bound kernel slices) + proxy buffering that holds chunks until a threshold. When the server yields for CPU, proxy decides to flush later, resulting in long inter-chunk pauses.

Immediate asks for data:
- Dawn: can you share a representative client-side trace showing request headers (Connection, TE, HTTP versions) and the timestamps of application read() calls?
- Halcyon ops: please keep one failing request's full TCP-level capture (you uploaded a short one — we may need a 30s window).

Planned mitigation steps (we can execute now):
A) Re-route Halcyon to non-canary pool (Marissa: please initiate).
B) Adjust nginx proxy to disable chunk buffering for that route (set proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; add tcp_nodelay).
C) Re-run a small controlled load to validate.

If the customer accepts a temporary non-streaming fallback, that will be the fastest user-visible mitigation. If we make the proxy change, expect ~10–15m to propagate.

—Sean
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
